explication:
<explanation>
1. Project Type & Purpose  
   - This is an open-source Go framework (library + CLI/HTTP servers) for building intelligent agent systems.  
   - It exposes a modular, layered API (packages) that you compose into “Runners” and “Agents,” integrates LLMs, tools, memory, knowledge, and telemetry.

2. High-Level Architecture & Main Components  
   Draw your diagram with these major containers (use color‐coding or swimlanes for “Core Library,” “Services/Stores,” and “External”):  
   A. Core Library  
     1. Runner  
        • Orchestrates end-to-end execution: session, telemetry, agent invocation, streaming events  
     2. Agent  
        • Interface implementations: LLMAgent, ChainAgent, ParallelAgent, CycleAgent, GraphAgent  
     3. Planner  
        • Decides strategy, tool selection, branching (chain/graph/cycle)  
     4. Executor  
        • Executes plan steps, invokes Tools or sub-Agents  
     5. Model Interface  
        • LLM wrappers (OpenAI, DeepSeek, etc.)  
     6. Tool Interface  
        • Tools: function, file ops, DuckDuckGo, MCP, code executor, etc.  
   B. Services & Stores  
     7. Session Service  
        • Manages per-user, per-session context and event streams (in-memory, Redis)  
     8. Memory Service  
        • Long-term storage of conversation state (in-memory, Redis)  
     9. Knowledge Service  
        • RAG: loaders, chunking, embedders, retrievers, vector stores (in-memory, elasticsearch, pgvector, tcvector)  
     10. Telemetry  
        • Tracing & metrics, hooks into runner/agent/model/tool layers, exporters (Langfuse, OpenTelemetry)  
   C. HTTP Servers & Examples  
     11. AGUI Server  
        • SSE endpoints for web UIs, adapter layer  
     12. A2A Server  
        • Agent-to-agent tunnel  
     13. Debug Server  
        • HTTP + OpenAPI, event replay  

3. Component Relationships & Data Flows  
   - Runner → Agent  
     • Runner invokes Agent.Run(…) → returns a stream of events  
   - Agent → Planner → Model / Knowledge / Memory  
     • Planner generates a plan (sequence or graph of steps)  
     • May consult Knowledge Service for RAG retrieval  
     • May fetch Memory context  
   - Executor → Tools / Sub-Agents  
     • Steps that call Tools (e.g., function tool calls local function)  
     • Or delegate to sub-Agents (ChainAgent, ParallelAgent, GraphAgent)  
   - Model ↔ External LLM API  
     • Model interface sends chat prompts, receives streamed responses  
   - Session / Memory → Storage  
     • Reads/Writes session state or memory entries to in-memory store or Redis/DB  
   - Telemetry wraps all calls, emits traces/metrics to exporters  
   - HTTP Servers expose Runner/Agent as REST/SSE endpoints, adapt requests into Runner.Run calls and stream events over HTTP  

4. Architectural Patterns & Design Principles  
   - Layered Modular Architecture: clear separation between orchestration (Runner), decision logic (Planner), execution (Executor), and I/O (Model, Tool, Services)  
   - Plugin/Interface-Driven: each core concept (Agent, Model, Tool, Session, Memory, Knowledge) is defined by an interface, enabling multiple implementations  
   - Adapter Pattern: Server packages adapt the core Runner/Agent API to HTTP/SSE or other protocols  
   - Composite Pattern: Multi-agent types (Chain, Parallel, Graph, Cycle) nest or parallelize sub-agents  
   - Dependency Injection: Users supply tools, memory services, telemetry configurations via functional options  

5. Tailoring the Diagram for an Open-Source Framework  
   - Emphasize extension points (interfaces for Agent, Model, Tool, Session, Memory, Knowledge)  
   - Show default implementations (in-memory, Redis, Elastic, PGVector, etc.) as pluggable modules  
   - Highlight example clients (CLI, AGUI web client, debug web UI) that wire into the core library  

6. Diagram Elements & Conventions  
   - Components: draw as labeled rectangles (group closely related packages)  
   - Data Stores / Services: use cylinder symbols for session/memory/knowledge stores  
   - External Systems: use cloud or cylinder symbols for LLM API, Redis, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL  
   - Arrows:  
     • Solid arrows for call/invocation flow (Runner → Agent → Planner → Executor → Tools / Model)  
     • Dashed arrows for data read/write (Agent → Memory Service → Redis)  
     • Bidirectional arrows for streaming (Model ↔ LLM API; Runner ↔ HTTP client)  
   - Color-Code Shapes:  
     • Core Library (blue rectangles)  
     • Services/Stores (green cylinders)  
     • External (gray clouds/cylinders)  
     • HTTP Servers & UI (orange rectangles)  

7. Step-by-Step Diagram Creation  
   1. Draw the Runner at the top center – it’s the entry point.  
   2. Under Runner, place Agent; under Agent, place Planner and Executor side by side.  
   3. From Planner, draw arrows to Model interface and Knowledge Service.  
   4. From Executor, draw arrows to Tool interface and to sub-Agent composite (Chain/Parallel/Graph).  
   5. Place Session and Memory stores to the left; draw dashed arrows from Runner/Agent to Session and Memory.  
   6. Place Telemetry alongside Runner/Agent/Model with arrows intercepting calls.  
   7. On the right, draw external LLM API, Redis/DB, Elasticsearch, showing arrow from Model → LLM API and Services → storage.  
   8. At the bottom or side, show HTTP Servers (AGUI, A2A, Debug) calling into Runner and streaming responses via SSE.  
   9. Legend: shapes, colors, arrow styles.  

By following these guidelines, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that highlights the core modules, data flows, extension points, and external integrations of the tRPC-Agent-Go framework.  
</explanation>
